newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-LOS ANGELES BEAT METROSTARS FOR FIRST ROAD WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LOS ANGELES BEAT METROSTARS FOR FIRST ROAD WIN.

text.p: Harut Karapetyan scored two goals to lead the Los Angeles Galaxy to their first road victory of the season, a 4-1 win over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars in Major League Soccer on Sunday.

Brazilian Welton and U.S. international midfielder Cobi Jones also scored for the Galaxy (7-11), who climbed out of last place in the Western Conference after having dropped eight consecutive away matches.

The MetroStars (6-12), in last place in the Eastern Conference, could not muster much of an attack. Before the match, the MetroStars announced they had acquired Brazilian World Cup star defender Branco.

In Tampa, Brazilian Gilmar broke a 1-1 tie to help boost the Tampa Bay Mutiny (11-10) to a 3-1 win over the San Jose Clash (7-14), who fell to last place in the Western Conference. Martin Vasquez and Roy Lassiter also tallied for the Mutiny, El Salvadoran Ronald Cerritos for the Clash.

In Columbus, Polish star Robert Warzycha scored his first goal of the season for the Columbus Crew (8-10), who posted a 1-0 win over the New England Revolution (12-8). The Crew had lost eight of their last nine games. Scott Coufal played in place of the Revolution's Italian goalkeeper Walter Zenga, who will miss from four to eight weeks after having knee surgery.

In Denver, the Dallas Burn (12-9) rallied from a 2-0 deficit behind two goals by Mexican Damian Alvarez to defeat the Colorado Rapids (9-11) 4-2, the team's second win in 48 hours. Uruguayan Adrian Paz scored both Rapids goals.
Dallas beat the San Jose Clash (7-14) 3-1 at home Friday as Dante Washington converted the Burn's first hat-trick to become the league's leading American scorer (nine goals and six assists).
In other action last weekend, the Kansas City Wizards (13-7) continued their domination of D.C. United (13-6) with a 3-2 home victory over the defending league champions.

Mark Chung scored twice and Preki set up all three goals in a confrontation of the two conference leaders. Zimbabwean Digital Takawira scored the game-winner four minutes into the second half for the Wizards, who are 5-0 lifetime vs. United.

Chung scored both of his goals within four minutes early in the game before United equalised on goals by U.S. National Team captain John Harkes and El Salvadoran international striker Raul Diaz Arce. Arce extended his MLS record point streak to 10 games.
In Foxboro, the Revolution overcame a 2-0 halftime deficit, scoring four unanswered goals in the second half on the way to a 4-2 win over the Mutiny.

After Lassiter and Vasquez had given the Mutiny a two-goal bulge, Chiquinho Conde took command of the match over four minutes. He set up Imad Baba's goal in the 53rd minute, then scored twice himself to lift New England in a 3-2 edge. John Kerr closed out the scoring.
